title: Synthetic two-signal example
summary: Figure 1 shows two invented signal values. Equation (1) uses them to calculate the ratio of signal B to signal A.

nodes.label: Two signals
nodes.summary: The example gives a value for each signal and calculates their ratio.
nodes.detail: Figure 1 identifies signals A and B. Equation (1) divides B by A.

nodes.label: Read Figure 1
nodes.summary: The two horizontal bars represent signals A and B.
nodes.detail: Use the caption to match each bar to its signal and value.

nodes.label: Read Equation (1)
nodes.summary: The ratio compares signal B with signal A.
nodes.detail: B goes in the numerator and A in the denominator.

nodes.label: Upper A, lower B
nodes.summary: The upper bar represents A and the lower bar represents B.
nodes.detail: The caption assigns 1 arbitrary unit to A and 2 arbitrary units to B.

nodes.label: Divide B by A
nodes.summary: Substitute the values into r = B/A.

nodes.label: A = 1 and B = 2
nodes.summary: Both signal values use arbitrary units.
nodes.detail: The bar caption and the ratio calculation use the same two values.

flow.title: Match each bar to its value
flow.action: Read the upper bar first, then the lower bar.
flow.output: Signal A is 1 arbitrary unit and signal B is 2 arbitrary units.
flow.role: These values supply the two inputs to Equation (1).

table.caption: Signal values from the Figure 1 caption

flow.title: Compute the ratio
flow.input: A = 1 and B = 2, in arbitrary units.
flow.action: Divide B by A in the order given in Equation (1).
flow.role: The ratio expresses B as a multiple of A.

depth.title: Which bar represents signal B?
depth.conclusion: The lower bar is signal B, with a value of 2 arbitrary units.
depth.mechanism: The caption identifies the signals by their vertical positions.
depth.evidence: Figure 1 assigns the upper bar to A (1 unit) and the lower bar to B (2 units).

figure.caption: Figure 1. The upper bar shows signal A (1 unit) and the lower bar shows signal B (2 units).

depth.title: How does Equation (1) give a ratio of 2?
depth.condition: Use A = 1 and B = 2 in the same arbitrary units.
depth.conclusion: Signal B is twice signal A in this example.
depth.mechanism: Place B in the numerator and A in the denominator. The common unit cancels in B/A.
